ans.protein_name: Aurora kinase Ipl1 (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) carrying a D227N substitution in the catalytic loop
ans.enzyme_family: Ser/Thr protein kinase, Aurora kinase subfamily

catalytic_residues.role: ATP alpha/beta-phosphate-binding lysine (beta3 VAIK-type motif, here ALK)
alphaC-helix glutamate forming the salt bridge with the beta3 lysine
catalytic-loop lysine contacting the ATP gamma-phosphate

substituted_or_missing.role: catalytic base aspartate of the HRD motif in the catalytic loop

ans.reason: The sequence matches the yeast Aurora kinase Ipl1 and keeps the glycine-rich loop (GKGKFGKV, 111-118), the beta3 lysine, the alphaC glutamate and the DFG motif, but the HRD catalytic-loop motif reads HRN (Asp227 to Asn). Loss of the catalytic base aspartate is a classic kinase-dead substitution, so phosphotransfer activity (EC 2.7.11.1 in the wild type) is expected to be abolished or nearly so.
